scope: Six assigned lymph-node/inflammation construction/support bodies, two whole parent contexts and four protected native variants; bounded source-asset inventory, not a replacement ordinary curriculum denominator.

units.requirement: Lymphatic vessels collect tissue fluid and ultimately return it to blood; vessels transport and nodes are organized organs, not passive pipes.

Afferent lymph enters the subcapsular sinus; efferent lymph leaves the medullary/hilar region toward further lymphatics before downstream return to blood. The pictured vein is not the lymph-return junction.

The node schematic locates capsule, subcapsular sinus, outer B-cell follicles, neighboring/deeper T-cell paracortex, medulla and hilar region; these are adjacent regions rather than sealed rooms, fixed proportions or one compulsory puncture point.

Soluble material and migrating dendritic cells can reach a draining node separately. Sixt tests earlier soluble-antigen access to resident DCs in mouse nodes; not every antigen must wait for a migrating DC.

One simplified blood branch connects arterial input through a capillary network to postcapillary HEV and venous output; blood lumens remain separate from lymph spaces. This is neither an artery-to-vein shortcut nor a complete exclusive vascular map.

Naive B and T lymphocytes can cross from HEV blood into node tissue; this is distinct from blood-flow and lymph-flow arrows. Red cells remain in blood, and not every circulating cell crosses or uses an artery-wall entry.

The HEV enlargement teaches the lumen-to-tissue side change without asserting an exclusive paracellular/transcellular path, rigid pocket, rolling receptor sequence or transit time. Fine enlargement/label leaders are not transport arrows.
Efferent lymph may carry recirculating lymphocytes, but the sketch specifies neither every cell class nor one mandatory cell path through medullary cords.

Draining denotes tissue territory, not cancer involvement. Enlargement and imaging do not establish malignancy; pathologic involvement concerns examined tissue, and a sampled negative node does not certify unsampled nodes.

Antigen arrival, uptake, relevant display and useful priming are different claims. An encounter can support activation or tolerance; arrival alone establishes neither tumor specificity nor useful cancer immunity.
Chemokines, receptors and adhesion help organize movement. CCR7 disruption altered organization and migration in mice, not a guarantee that adding one cue yields useful immunity.
Imaging location/shape/dimensions, drainage mapping, sampled-tissue pathology and controlled immune response measurements answer different questions; record node, time, collection and region.
A tertiary lymphoid structure is organized immune tissue outside native lymphoid organs and is not another name for a lymph node.
The fictional earlier soluble-antigen arrival before antigen-carrying DCs is possible but does not prove presentation, antigen-dependent activation or cancer-cell involvement.

Blood and lymph are connected circulation systems rather than interchangeable samples; schematic colors, cell counts and route geometry provide no rates, scales, breast-staging map or treatment recommendation.

Inflammation is a tissue response to infection, injury or tissue stress/disturbed function, with multiple causes and cells. Sterile inflammation can occur without an initiating infection; the word does not imply an automatically helpful response.
Local signals can change vascular permeability and cell trafficking, recruiting leukocytes and admitting fluid/proteins. The separate cell-entry and fluid/protein arrows do not depict angiogenesis.
Responders can contain problems, clear material or support repair, or signaling can persist with further injury. The schematic provides no measured time course or inevitable sequence/outcome.
Resolution involves coordinated biological processes rather than every responder simply becoming inactive together.

Macrophage states depend on local signal combinations; M1/M2 are simplified experimental poles, not universal boxes for human tissue cells. Marker panels or RNA scores are not complete functional identities.
Acute/chronic time course and local/systemic distribution are different axes, not interchangeable triggers, consequences or treatment mechanisms.
Woo and Bakhoum report context-dependent antitumor versus metastatic DNA-sensing mechanisms in different experimental systems, not a head-to-head clinical comparison.
Inflammation after an intervention, immunogenic cell death, antigen-specific recognition of untreated cancer cells, killing and clinical benefit require separate evidence.

Tissue-cell patterns, RNA programs, protein concentrations and clinical observations are different measurements with different units and denominators. Report specimen/time/quantity; one marker does not identify cause or every producing cell.
The fictional treatment-associated swelling and inflammatory RNA signal alone show a local response, leaving cause, responder identity, antigen-specific recognition and useful function open.
